Class AizawaEquations

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.mdi3D.view3D.aizawaDemo.AizawaEquations
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.apache.commons.math3.ode.FirstOrderDifferentialEquations
public class AizawaEquations extends Object implements org.apache.commons.math3.ode.FirstOrderDifferentialEquations
Implements the six-parameter Aizawa attractor as a system of three first-order ordinary differential equations.

The state vector is: 

y[0] = x
y[1] = y
y[2] = z
and the governing equations are: 
dx/dt = (z - b) x - d y
dy/dt = d x + (z - b) y
dz/dt = c + a z - z^3 / 3 - (x^2 + y^2)(1 + e z) + f z x^3
This is the more commonly used Aizawa system for the familiar strange-attractor visualizations.

The class is immutable and thread-safe after construction.

    • AizawaEquations

    • AizawaEquations

      public AizawaEquations(double a, double b, double c, double d, double e, double f)
      Creates an Aizawa system with the specified parameter values.
      Parameters:
      a - the linear coefficient multiplying z in dz/dt
      b - the shift applied to z in the x and y equations
      c - the constant driving term in dz/dt
      d - the rotation-like coupling between x and y
      e - the coefficient in the nonlinear factor (1 + e z)
      f - the coefficient of the nonlinear term z x^3 in dz/dt

  • Method Details

    • defaultInitialState

      public static double[] defaultInitialState()
      Returns a fresh default initial state for integrations of this system.

      A new array is returned on each call so that client code can modify the returned state safely without changing shared static data.

      Returns:
      a new three-element array containing a standard initial condition

    • computeDerivatives

      public void computeDerivatives(double t, double[] y, double[] yDot) throws org.apache.commons.math3.exception.MaxCountExceededException
      Computes the time derivatives of the Aizawa state vector.

      The input state array is interpreted as: 

      state[0] = x
state[1] = y
state[2] = z
      and the output derivative array is filled as: 
      yDot[0] = dx/dt
yDot[1] = dy/dt
yDot[2] = dz/dt
      Specified by:
      computeDerivatives in interface org.apache.commons.math3.ode.FirstOrderDifferentialEquations
      Parameters:
      t - the independent variable, usually time; unused here because the system is autonomous
      y - the current state vector
      yDot - the array to receive the computed derivatives
      Throws:
      org.apache.commons.math3.exception.MaxCountExceededException - if the Commons Math integrator signals an evaluation limit problem
